item.mechanism: Laves phase precipitation reduces atomic radii misfit and lowers the elastic energy of the solid solution, driving phase decomposition from the single-phase BCC structure.
item.system: CrMoNbWV high-entropy alloy (equiatomic) produced by mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering (SPS)
item.operating_conditions: SPS at 1200–1400 °C; presence of Fe impurities (3.5 wt.% from milling balls); room temperature for mechanical testing
item.supporting_observation: The volume fraction of Laves phases (Cr2Nb, (Fe,Cr)Nb) was 41.6 vol.% at 1200 °C and decreased to 11.5 vol.% at 1400 °C, while the BCC matrix remained.
item.scope_limits: Does not hold for the initial MA powder which was a single-phase BCC solid solution; the mechanism is specific to the SPS process where decomposition occurs.
item.alternatives_considered: Single-phase solid solution formation predicted by high mixing entropy and thermodynamic parameters (δ ≤ 6.6%, Ω > 1.1, VEC = 5.6).
quotes: The Laves phase precipitation reduces the atomic radii misfit and reduces the CrMoNbWV solid solution's elastic energy.

In the present paper, the MA allowed to obtain a CrMoNbWV alloy with a single-phase BCC structure. However, the following SPS leads to partial decomposition of the solid solution and precipitation of the Laves phases
The Laves phase formation is consistent with the triple Nb-Cr-Fe phase diagram.

item.mechanism: High volume fraction of brittle Laves phases and oxides localized at grain boundaries promotes crack initiation and propagation, causing low plasticity.
item.operating_conditions: Room temperature compressive testing; sintering temperatures of 1200 °C and 1300 °C
item.supporting_observation: Samples exhibited compressive strength of 2700–2870 MPa but low plasticity; microstructure showed Laves phases and oxides at grain boundaries.
item.scope_limits: At 1400 °C, while Laves fraction decreases, coarse oxide particles become the dominant crack initiation source, maintaining low plasticity.
item.alternatives_considered: Grain boundary hardening and solid solution hardening which increase strength but do not explain the specific brittleness mechanism.
quotes: These phases were brittle at room temperature, and their localization promoted a crack initiation and propagation along the grain boundaries resulting in a decrease of the HEA plasticity.
The coarse inclusions can act as a crack initiation source and cause fractures in the BCC-matrix that leads to a decrease of the HEA plasticity.

item.mechanism: Grain boundary hardening (Hall–Petch) and solid solution hardening due to lattice strains from substitutional and interstitial elements increase compressive strength.
item.system: CrMoNbWV HEA produced by mechanical alloying and SPS
item.operating_conditions: Room temperature; sintering temperatures 1200–1400 °C; presence of interstitial C and O
item.supporting_observation: Compressive strength of 2700–2870 MPa was achieved, attributed to fine grains (<15 µm) and lattice strains from C and O intercalation.
item.scope_limits: Strength does not significantly increase with sintering temperature despite grain growth, suggesting competing effects of grain coarsening and phase dissolution.
item.alternatives_considered: Precipitation hardening by Laves phases and oxides, which also contribute but are linked to brittleness.
quotes: The high strength values of samples obtained by powder metallurgy methods can be explained by the influence of the following hardening mechanisms: (1) grain boundary hardening described by Hall–Petch relationship; (2) solid solution hardening due to strong lattice strains caused by substitutional elements; (3) solid solution hardening by interstitial elements

Compared to a coarse-grained structure of the HEA obtained by melting, the CrMoNbWV HEA, obtained by SPS of the MA-powder, has a structure with equiaxial grains with a size of less than 15 µm. This fact provides the grain boundary hardening of the BCC-matrix.
The intercalation of carbon atoms to the HEA BCC structure leads to lattice strains and the formation of some amount of fine-dispersed HEA carbides.

item.mechanism: Reverse dissolution of Laves phases occurs at higher temperatures due to the increased influence of the entropy component (ΔS_mix) over the enthalpy component (ΔH_mix).
item.supporting_observation: Laves phase volume fraction decreased from 41.6% (1200 °C) to 11.5% (1400 °C), with the phase almost absent at 1400 °C.
item.scope_limits: This mechanism explains the reduction of Laves phases but does not account for the coarsening of oxide particles which occurs simultaneously.
item.alternatives_considered: Simple diffusion of elements without thermodynamic driving force changes.
quotes: The increase of the SPS temperature leads to reverse dissolution of the Laves phases in the solid solution that is possibly connected with the higher influence of entropy component ΔS mix than the enthalpy one ΔH mix in this case.
In addition, the increase of the sintering temperature promotes a higher diffusion of elements in the alloy.

item.mechanism: Carburization of the surface layer due to interaction with the graphite die creates lattice strains and fine carbides, significantly enhancing wear resistance.
item.system: Surface layer of CrMoNbWV HEA sintered at 1200–1400 °C
item.operating_conditions: SPS in graphite die; abrasive wear testing (ASTM G65); room temperature
item.supporting_observation: Carburized layer bulk loss (0.001 cm³) was lower than bulk HEA (0.0035–0.0048 cm³) and nickel-bonded tungsten carbide; layer thickness 18–75 µm.
item.scope_limits: The mechanism is specific to the carburized surface layer; the bulk material has lower wear resistance than the carburized layer.
item.alternatives_considered: Wear resistance of the bulk HEA attributed to the BCC matrix and Laves phases, which is lower than the carburized layer.
quotes: When investigating the sample cross-sections in detail, it was determined that under SPS, the HEA powder interacted with the carbon of the equipment that led to carburization of the surface layer.
The XRD showed that under sintering, carbon atoms were intercalated to the HEA BCC-lattice that led to strains in the latter and the formation of some HEA carbides.
The higher characteristics of the carburized layer probably result from the BCC-lattice strain caused by the intercalation of carbon atoms and the fine-dispersed HEA carbides.

item.mechanism: Corrosion resistance is enhanced by the formation of protective passive films on the surface composed of oxides of Nb, Mo, V, and Cr.
item.operating_conditions: Electrochemical testing in 0.5 M H2SO4 solution at room temperature; ambient aeration
item.supporting_observation: Corrosion current density (i_corr) values were low (0.20–2.81 µA/cm²); positive shift in E_OCP with increasing sintering temperature.
item.scope_limits: Selective dissolution occurs at Laves phases ((Fe,Cr)Nb and Cr2Nb), indicating these regions are less resistant than the BCC matrix.
item.alternatives_considered: Depletion of Mo and Cr in the matrix due to σ-phase formation (mentioned as a general risk in HEAs, though not the primary mechanism here).
quotes: The sintered samples exhibit a low corrosion rate connected with the strong passivation ability of Nb, Mo, V, and Cr.
These elements can form protective passivating coatings on the alloy surface in acid solutions.

item.mechanism: Coarse oxide particles formed at higher sintering temperatures act as crack initiation sources, reducing plasticity despite lower Laves phase content.
item.operating_conditions: SPS at 1400 °C; room temperature compressive testing
item.supporting_observation: At 1400 °C, Laves phase content was low (11.5%), but oxide particle size increased significantly, and plasticity remained low.
item.scope_limits: This mechanism competes with the beneficial effect of reduced Laves phase content; it explains why strength does not improve significantly at 1400 °C.
item.alternatives_considered: Grain coarsening leading to decreased hardness, which is a separate mechanism affecting mechanical properties.
quotes: In the sample sintered at 1400 °C, the volume fraction of the Laves phases is lowered. However, the particle size of the oxides increases significantly.
The coarse inclusions can serve as sources of crack initiation in the BCC-matrix.
The increase of the sintering temperature led to changes in oxide morphology: it became circular instead of splintery (polyangular).

item.mechanism: Wear resistance of the carburized layer is proportional to its hardness, following the Archard wear equation, due to lattice strains and carbide formation.
item.system: Carburized surface layer of CrMoNbWV HEA
item.operating_conditions: Abrasive wear testing (ASTM G65) with silica sand; room temperature
item.supporting_observation: Bulk loss of carburized layer was 300% lower than bulk HEA; wear rate difference corresponds to hardness differences.
item.scope_limits: The mechanism applies specifically to the carburized layer; the bulk HEA wear resistance is lower and attributed to the BCC matrix and Laves phases.
item.alternatives_considered: Wear resistance of the bulk HEA compared to conventional composites (SiC, SiC/B4C) which is also high but lower than the carburized layer.
quotes: The difference between the values for the carburized layer and the bulk HEA is 300%, indicating the superior wear resistance of the carburized layer compared to the conventional hard alloys.
According to the equation, sliding wear resistance is proportional to the alloy hardness.
The higher characteristics of the carburized layer probably result from the BCC-lattice strain caused by the intercalation of carbon atoms and the fine-dispersed HEA carbides.
